title: SharePoint: Governance Reviews Dashboard for site owners
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and documented lifecycle policy behaviour are supported, and dashboard-specific gaps remain unfilled in the sources searched. Two policy paths need minor completion, but their printed steps are correct and lead to the right wizard.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model rests on SharePoint's general requirement that users have a licence including SharePoint.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published dashboard-specific licensing requirements, including whether the SAM prerequisites also apply.
claims.quote: Searched: "Governance Reviews Dashboard" SharePoint license price prerequisites meter; read SAM prerequisites, SharePoint service description and roadmap, and searched policy pages for the dashboard. General SharePoint and SAM requirements exist; no dashboard-specific requirement found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a dashboard-specific price.
claims.quote: Searched: "Governance Reviews Dashboard" SharePoint license price prerequisites meter; read SAM prerequisites and SharePoint service description and inspected search results. No price for the dashboard found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: SAM prerequisites require one of the listed Office 365, Microsoft 365 or government base subscriptions.
claims.quote: Your organization must have one of the following base licenses: Office 365 E3, E5, or A5; Microsoft 365 E1, E3, E5, or A5; Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC-High, or DoD

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: At least one user assigned a Microsoft Copilot licence is one route to the documented SAM capabilities.
claims.quote: At least one user in your organization is assigned a Microsoft Copilot license. (The user doesn't need to be a SharePoint administrator.)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A subscription including SharePoint K, P1 or P2 plus the SAM Plan 1 add-on is another documented licensing route.
claims.quote: Your subscription includes SharePoint K, P1, or P2, and your organization purchases the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 is another documented route to SAM capabilities.
claims.quote: Your organization has Microsoft 365 E7, also known as The Frontier Suite.

claims.where: Governance guidance / At rollout
claims.claim: Learn recommends avoiding overlapping scopes for policies of the same type because notification schedules and enforcement become harder to predict.
claims.quote: We recommend that policies of the same type don't have overlapping scopes. If sites fall under multiple policies of the same type, notification schedules and enforcement actions can become difficult to predict.

claims.where: Governance guidance / After rollout
claims.claim: Lifecycle policies generate execution reports that administrators can use to monitor review outcomes.
claims.quote: Each policy execution generates reports that help administrators understand policy outcomes and identify sites that require attention.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Policies of different types notify independently.
claims.quote: Policies of different types operate independently for notification purposes. Notification history is tracked separately for each policy type.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling or deleting a policy stops its future notifications and enforcement actions.
claims.quote: Disabling or deleting a policy stops future activities from that policy, including notifications and enforcement actions.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling or deleting a policy does not reverse actions already applied.
claims.quote: It doesn't automatically reverse previously applied actions.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].note; Governance controls / inactive row
claims.claim: The inactive policy scope is reached through Policies > Site lifecycle management > Inactive site policies > Open > + Create policy > Set policy scope in the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: Under Inactive site policies, select Open. ... Select + Create policy. Review the Manage inactive sites information, and then select Next. ... On the Set policy scope step, choose your policy scope option
claims.fix: Set controls[2].ui.path and the corresponding rendered table path to 'Policies > Site lifecycle management > Inactive site policies > Open > + Create policy > Manage inactive sites > Set policy scope', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/inactive-site-policy.
